name: Stacked Timeline Versioning
use_when: A short or reel has many source clips and multiple possible durations.
The editor needs to compare an original, shorter, and balanced version without losing work.
The cut needs pacing judgment before effects, captions, or color are finalized.
avoid_when: The task is a tiny trim or one-off export.
The software setup makes stacked timelines slow or confusing and duplicate sequences would be clearer.
The editor has not named versions clearly enough to avoid exporting the wrong one.

timeline_pattern.pattern: original_assembly -> duplicate_shorter_version -> duplicate_balanced_version -> compare_stacked_or_side_by_side -> choose_lock -> polish
timeline_pattern.version_rule: Keep every major pacing experiment in a named version instead of destructively trimming the only timeline.
timeline_pattern.balance_rule: The best short is not always the shortest; choose the version with the strongest story, connection, and retention balance.
timeline_pattern.lock_rule: Do not spend major polish on a version until the chosen duration and order are clear.

motion.rule: Do not judge motion polish until the version's cut order and duration are stable.

sound.rule: When comparing versions, check that dialogue, music, foley, and SFX still sync after ripple trims.

captions.rule: Caption timing belongs on the chosen or near-chosen version so repeated versioning does not create caption churn.

color.rule: Save heavy look work for the selected version; basic correction can be copied after lock.

implementation.ffmpeg: Represent each version as a separate EDL or concat list and render short comparison previews before applying final filters.
implementation.remotion: Store candidate cuts as named timeline arrays such as original, short, and balanced, then choose one as activeComposition.
implementation.blender: Duplicate timeline scenes or strips for major timing variants and lock the chosen scene before compositing.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Duplicate the project or timeline before major trimming and label versions by duration/purpose.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Duplicate sequences for original, short, and balanced versions; use markers and sequence names to prevent wrong-version export.

common_mistakes: Destroying the original cut before knowing whether the shorter version works.
Choosing the shortest version even when it removes the human or emotional reason to keep watching.
Polishing captions, effects, or color on a version that is still structurally uncertain.
Exporting the wrong sequence because versions are not clearly named.
Failing to re-check audio and captions after moving clips between versions.
qc: Are original, shorter, and balanced versions named and recoverable?
Was the final version chosen for story and retention rather than shortest duration alone?
Are captions, SFX, music, and B-roll still synced after version changes?
Is heavy polish applied only to the chosen or near-locked version?
Does the export come from the intended named version?
